corta: the key panel runs off all four edges of the frame — no desk, no room, no whole device is ever visible, only the keys themselves filling the picture edge to edge
escena: SCENE (support desk, extreme macro, night): a dense grid of small square response keys fills the ENTIRE frame, cropped hard on every side. Every key carries its own worn label and a faint glowing cool blue backlight: they are the ready-made answers, used thousands of times, their edges polished smooth by years of thumbs. Dead centre, ONE key is BLANK — no label, no wear, its backlight dark. It is the only unlit, unmarked key in the whole grid and it sits exactly where the eye lands. A single fingertip hovers just above that blank key, not pressing it, the only piece of a person in frame and cut by the edge. A hard low raking light from the left throws sharp graphic shadows down the side of every key, very high contrast, the far side of the grid falling to near black. A small orange sculpture rests at the top right corner of the grid, cropped by the edge, catching the raking light. 100mm macro lens at f/4, focus on the blank key. The whole frame is COOL and contemporary: daylight-neutral white balance, blue-leaning shadows, nothing warm, amber, golden or tungsten anywhere, no retro glow — the ONLY warm colour in the entire picture is the small orange sculpture itself. Everything except the sculpture is completely unbranded, and no text anywhere is readable: the key labels are worn, angled and shallow-focused — legible as marks, never as words.

lecho.objeto: the out-of-focus near row of keys running along the very bottom, right against the lens and outside the raking light

texto.muro: the dark unlit upper rows of the same key grid, evenly toned and free of backlight, their matte plastic texture visible
